name: Northern Pacific main line (as in 1883)
built_text: 1880 (track reached the Little Missouri in 1880; bridge under construction in Haynes 1880 photo)
evidence: West of the river, today's BNSF (former NP) track falls exactly on the track drawn on the 1883 plat. East of the river the plat draws the track up to ~100 m south of today's line, south of a row of blocks that today lies north of the track. Either the plat is schematic there or the line was later realigned - check NP valuation and right-of-way maps (MNHS).
sources: PLAT1883; OSM; HAG ch. I

name: Northern Pacific bridge (trestle) over the Little Missouri
evidence: Where the track crosses the 1883 channel traced from the plat. HAG: the train "rumbled across three hundred feet of trestle." People crossed on foot between the rails at high water (HAG).
sources: PLAT1883; HAG ch. I; Bismarck Weekly Tribune 1885-10-16 (an NP bridge west of Medora burned)
photos: mhs:91737 (under construction, 1880); mhs:95324; mhs:72459 (Huffman 1886, "Medora from railway bridge"); shsnd:00042-00151

name: Ford of the Little Missouri
built_text: in use 1883
evidence: "the ford a hundred yards north of the trestle" (HAG ch. I). Placed 100 yd north of the 1883 crossing.
sources: HAG ch. I

name: Bad Lands Cantonment (abandoned army post)
removed_text: part burned early 1887; rest razed or hauled away; hospital moved to Dickinson fall 1888
use: army post 1879-83; ranch HQ, resort, homes and church services 1883-86
footprint_ft: barracks 200x22; officers' quarters 124x30; hospital 52x25 + 23x14; storehouse 100x22; laundresses 41x28; guardhouse 25x30; bakery 30x20; blacksmith 18x18; stables 54x38; ice house 30x25; two cellars 18x16
evidence: Eight building symbols drawn on the 1883 plat, labelled "Cantonments," NW of the river crossing. HM52: about 3/4 mile NW of Medora under the bluffs; buildings ranged round a central parade ground (Lang). Symbols are schematic, so individual buildings are not identified.
sources: PLAT1883; HM52 pp. 10-11 (building sizes, from post Letters Sent, 1 Jan 1880); TRC-CANT; LANG; NARA RG77 file unit 4522386 (7 building plans); SHSND MAP.032-00111 (1879 reserve map); HAG ch. I-II
notes: Dates conflict: established spring 1879 (TRC) vs Nov 10 1879 (HM52, HMdb); abandoned March 24 (TRC) vs March 4, 1883 (HMdb). SHSND surveyed the site with drone and magnetometry in June 2025 (PAC-MAC 2025 paper) - request the results. HAG puts it "a quarter of a mile west" of Maunders's shack; the plat puts it ~0.5 mi NW of the crossing. Cow Boy 1884-85: the buildings housed the Hyde, Hannigan, Butler, McGregor and Barker families and contractor J. A. Freeze; attached and sold by the sheriff July-Oct 1885; sold at sheriff's sale to Beckett & Foote of Dickinson 1888-89 (Dickinson Press, in HM52). BROOKS57: state highway gravel operations "destroyed the site" before 1952. A sutler's store (Frank Moore) stood on the parade ground: "long and low," with an L used as a bar and sleeping quarters behind (Huidekoper, in HM52).

name: Little Missouri depot
removed_text: replaced when NP trains began stopping at Medora (1884); later sold and moved to the HT Ranch
use: railroad station; NP Express and Western Union office
evidence: Beside the track on the west bank. Fitzgerald's shack was "directly to the east, on the brink of the river" (HAG), so the depot was close to the river; placed 150 m NW of the 1883 crossing, near where the 1957 NPS Tour of Medora map marks the site of Little Missouri (west end of the old US 10 bridge). Long side parallel to the track, as in Haynes's 1881 photo. Size is a placeholder.
sources: HAG ch. I; LANG; HMdb 87982; Dickinson Press 1883-09-22 ("the new depot will soon be completed")
photos: mhs:108837 (Haynes "Bad Land City," fall 1881); shsnd:00119-00017; shsnd:2003-P-010-00092b (after its move to the HT Ranch)
notes: "Too wide to fit through the railroad bridges," so it was sold rather than moved (HMdb 87982). A "new depot" was being finished in Sept 1883, so there may have been two buildings.

name: Pyramid Park Hotel
aka: Moore's hotel; the loft was "the bull-pen"
built_text: completed Nov 1880 by Frank Moore & Co. (HM52); "will soon be enlarged" (Bismarck Tribune 1882-10-06)
footprint_ft: not recorded; Haynes 1881 photo shows a 2-story front-gabled main block with a 2-story gabled block attached behind (L or T plan)
evidence: "stood immediately north of the tracks" (HAG); T.R. walked "northeastward" to it from the depot (HAG). Haynes's 1881 photo shows it beside the depot.
sources: HAG ch. I; AUTO ch. IV [P]; LANG; HM52; Bismarck Tribune 1882-10-06, 1883-06-15 (holds 30-40); TRC-CANT; HMdb 154619 ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-02-28, 1884-10, 1885-03; HM52 pp. 20, 25-26; BROOKS57 Fig. 3
photos: mhs:108837 (Haynes, fall 1881: two-story frame building with porch); shsnd:00119-00017; npshb:thro10.jpg
notes: T.R.'s first night in the Badlands, Sept 7-8, 1883. Fate unknown. Size is a placeholder until the Haynes photo is studied. Still operating 1884-85: second floor cut into rooms (Cow Boy 1884-02-28); reopened by Boyd & Alexander Oct 1884; Arch Boyd early 1885; J. B. Walker from March 1885 (Cow Boy). Lang calls it "recently erected" in April 1883 - perhaps the 1882-83 enlargement. In 1883 Moore also let rooms in the old Cantonment officers' quarters (Mandan Daily Pioneer 1883-07-17, in HM52).

name: Pennell & Roberts's saloon and billiard hall, Little Missouri ("Bill Williams's" in Hagedorn)
removed_text: Roberts & Co. moved the billiard hall to Roberts Hall in Medora, July 3, 1884 (Cow Boy)
evidence: "beside it [the hotel] stood the one-story palace of sin" (HAG); "near it stood Big-Mouthed Bob's" (LANG).
sources: HAG ch. I; LANG ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-02, 1884-04, 1884-07-03
notes: Hagedorn says "one, who shall, for the purposes of this story, be known as Bill Williams" - a pseudonym. Lang's "Big-Mouthed Bob" and the Roberts & Co. saloon at Medora (burned Jan 1885) suggest the real owner was Robert Roberts. Inference; verify. Pennell & Roberts's hall at Little Missouri hosted the stockmen's meetings of Feb and Apr 1884 (Cow Boy).

name: Johnny Nelson's store
built_text: by Sept 1883
evidence: "South of the track" (HAG ch. I). Lang: "three or four rough shacks" across the track at the base of "Graveyard Butte."
sources: HAG ch. I; LANG ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-03-27, 1884-06-26, 1884-10-02
notes: Joe Ferris's dry-goods store opened in "the former John Nelson building" (Cow Boy 1884-03-27), apparently on the west side; Ferris added a large addition (June 1884) and a warehouse (Oct 1884), then moved to his new Medora store in Aug 1885.

name: Mrs. McGeeney's boarding house
built_text: by Sept 1883
evidence: "next door" to Nelson's store; within fifty feet of Mrs. Fitzgerald (HAG ch. I, III).
sources: HAG ch. I and III

name: Section foreman Fitzgerald's shack
built_text: by Sept 1883
evidence: "Directly to the east, on the brink of the river" (HAG). Within 50 ft of McGeeney's, so placed south of the track.
sources: HAG ch. I and III

name: Jake Maunders's shack
built_text: by Sept 1883
evidence: "At a corresponding place on the other side of the track" from Fitzgerald (HAG ch. I).
sources: HAG ch. I

name: NP section house and water tank
evidence: "A little further along the track to the westward, stood a section house and water tank" (LANG). The 1879 Cantonment reserve map ties its bounds to the NP water tank (SHSND MAP.032-00111) - that map can fix this point.
sources: LANG; HMdb 87982; SHSND MAP.032-00111

name: Peter Malloy's hotel (the Western House?)
built_text: contract to James Collister Aug 1883; C. E. Cook carpenter (Dickinson Press)
evidence: "James Collister has the contract for erecting a fine hotel for Peter Malloy at Little Missouri" (Dickinson Press 1883-08-18). Location not given.
sources: Dickinson Press 1883-08-18, 09-15, 09-22; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-07-16
notes: Possibly the "Western House" Mrs. Malloy left in July 1885 for a new building on Main Street, Medora. The "Malloy building at Medora" was torn down and moved to Dickinson in June 1887 (Dickinson Press 1887-06-18). HAG calls the owner "P. McGeeney" when quoting the same 1883 note - check.

name: Chateau de Mores
built_text: 1883 (ready "by August" per BROOKS57; SHSND says ready for Medora in spring 1884)
material: frame; milled siding painted "French grey," red shingle roof, red shutters
footprint_ft: 26 rooms; OSM outline ~5,550 sq ft incl. veranda
evidence: Standing on its original site on the second terrace above the river, about half a mile WSW of Medora (NRHP).
sources: NRHP 75001299; SHSND Chateau history; SAH ND-01-BI8; PLAT1883 ("Marquis de Mores") ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-06, 1885-03, 1885-11-26
photos: shsnd:00042-00152; shsnd:00042-00158 (Ingersoll 1883); shsnd:00042-00157 (1884); shsnd:00042-00196/-00197 (1886); mhs:72389; mhs:72403 (Huffman 1886); houghton:3013538; shsnd:1972.91 (Medora de Mores watercolor)
notes: Drone photogrammetry model of the Chateau today (Sketchfab, 2023) - cleared for Library use. Color conflict: Cow Boy 1885-11-26 describes "green sides and red roof"; the 1974 NRHP gives "French grey" siding with red roof and shutters (the 1930s restoration color). Windmill added 1884; Peter Book built a cellar for the heating plant in 1885 (Cow Boy).

name: Chateau outbuildings (coachman's house, carriage shed, stable, corral; woodshed)
evidence: Woodshed north of the house; "to the south and further east, on the next terrace towards the river," the coachman's house, carriage shed, stable and corral (NRHP). Ingersoll's 1883 photo shows the carriage house below the Chateau.

name: Vegetable garden and irrigation ditch
evidence: Drawn and labelled "Vegetable Garden" with an irrigation ditch on the 1883 plat, south of the Chateau.
sources: PLAT1883

name: Coal mine
evidence: Labelled "Coal Mine" on the 1883 plat.
sources: PLAT1883

name: De Mores packing plant: chimney
aka: Northern Pacific Refrigerator Car Co. slaughter house
built_text: brick smokestack built by Peter Book, finished June 18, 1885 (Cow Boy); the plant itself: first abattoir Oct 1883, new plant opened June 2, 1885
removed_text: closed Nov 1886; used for storage; burned March 17, 1907; chimney stands
use: slaughterhouse, cold storage, ice houses, loading platform, holding pens
material: frame; brick chimney; sandstone and brick foundations
footprint_ft: chimney only; see the other packing-plant features
evidence: Chimney and foundations survive in Chimney Park (SHSND), at the "Slaughter House" drawn on the 1883 plat beside the track. Building footprints not yet laid out; the 1956 De Haven site plan in BROOKS57 p. 25 shows the abattoir site, a separate packing-house foundation and the holding pens.
sources: NRHP 75001300; PLAT1883; HAG; BROOKS57; HMdb 87796, 87799; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12-04, 1885-01-01, 1885-04-16; Dickinson Press 1883-09-22; St. Paul Daily Globe 1885-06-05 ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-03-26, 1885-06-18; BROOKS57 pp. 4, 17-19 and Fig. 6
notes: Capacity varies by source: 100 head/day (HAG), 150 (NRHP), 200 (Dickinson Press 1883 claim). Spring 1887 flood surrounded the slaughter houses (Bismarck Weekly Tribune 1887-03-18). Drone photogrammetry model of Chimney Park today (Sketchfab, 2023) - cleared for Library use. BROOKS57: the new plant was finished about mid-April 1885 "except for the smoke stack," so an 1883-84 view should not show the chimney. Capacity 900 head a week (Cow Boy). SHSND 00042-00153 is captioned "de Mores Packing Plant, Medora, N.D. 1883" on the card but shows a tall stack; either the caption date is later than the photo, or the 1883 plant had a stack of its own before Peter Book's 1885 chimney. Huffman 1886 (MHS 72460, 72459) and SHSND 00042-00074/-00075 (1885) show the finished plant.

name: Northern Pacific depot, Medora
built_text: 1884 (NP trains began stopping at Medora)
evidence: "near today's Medora Convenience Store" (HMdb 87986). Huffman's 1886 photo (MHS 72461) shows a one-and-a-half-story board-and-batten depot with its long side along the track, a bay window for the agent facing the track, a "MEDORA" sign with mileboards, and a covered freight end; HMdb's "perpendicular to the tracks" does not fit that photo. In the 1885-86 overviews a depot-sized building and loading sheds back-project within about 15-45 m of this spot.
notes: "A few steps" from the Hotel de Mores (Cow Boy). Used for church services and Sunday school. Size still a placeholder (about 24 x 60 ft from the photo's proportions). MHS dates its Huffman print to 1886 but the caption says "North Dakota" (statehood 1889), so the caption at least is later; confirm the date of the negative.

name: Hotel de Mores (Northern Pacific Hotel from 1885)
built_text: 1883, as a boarding house for up to 100 (HMdb); in use by Feb 1884 (Cow Boy); brick-veneered and reopened June 1, 1885
use: hotel, with livery stable and bar
evidence: Probably building "D" of the 1885 bird's-eye view, triangulated from SHSND 00042-00071 and 00042-00195; the reprojected base agrees with both photos (5 px and 2 px), and swapping D with D2 fails that test by about 60 px. Triangulated from two or more solved photos; sight lines cross within about 1-3 m, so the position is good to roughly +/-10 m once picking error is allowed for. Why the hotel: (1) a long two-story building with evenly spaced windows on both floors, the shape of the 1883 frame hotel (SHSND 00042-00149); (2) about 60 m north-east of the depot site - "a few steps from the depot" (Fitzgerald's ad, Cow Boy 1884); (3) long side facing north (HMdb 88037: "faced north"), with its west end on Main Street, which fits the race track running to "Main street opposite the Northern Pacific hotel" (Cow Boy) and the 1885 porch on the west side; (4) gone in the c.1905 postcard - the hotel burned in 1897. Location graded C because it rests on this identification.
sources: HMdb 88037; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-02-14, 1884-04-17; HAG (Mandan Pioneer: "a large hotel") ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-10-23, 1885-02 to 1885-06-04 ; SHSND 00042-00149, 00042-00071, 00042-00195 (camera solutions, docs/photo-matching.md); Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-02-07 (Fitzgerald ad)
photos: shsnd:00042-00076; shsnd:00042-00086 (1885); houghton:3013534; houghton:3013529 (interior); houghton:3013559 (1895); shsnd:00042-00149 (1883?, wood-sided) ; shsnd:00042-00071 (1885 bird's-eye, camera solved); shsnd:00042-00195 (1885-86 overview, camera solved); shsnd:00042-00194 (1885-86 overview, same camera station as -00195)
notes: SHSND 00042-00149 shows a wood-sided hotel in snow in 1883 - consistent with brick veneer added in 1885. 1885 rebuild (Cow Boy, Feb-May 1885): new foundations, brick veneer by Peter Book, porches on the west and south sides, kitchen and laundry additions on the north side; lessee Arch Boyd; renamed the Northern Pacific Hotel June 4, 1885. Earlier managed by G. W. Fitzgerald. Arson attempt Oct 23, 1884. Open conflict: in the 1885-86 overviews this building reads as white or light-painted, with an outside stair at its east end, while the Cow Boy says the hotel was brick-veneered in spring 1885 and SHSND 00042-00076 shows a long brick building. Either the overviews predate the veneer, the brick read light, or the brick building is a different structure. The site falls on the block the 1957 NPS Tour map shows as De Mores Memorial Park; whether the memorial park was laid out on the old hotel site is worth checking.

name: Roberts Hall (billiard hall and theatre)
aka: possibly Hagedorn's two-story "Bill Williams's" saloon and hall; possibly the 1903 "town hall"
built_text: April-June 1884; builder Thomas McClung (HMdb)
use: bar and club rooms below; hall with stage, two dressing rooms above; later county offices
material: frame; drop siding, board paper, plastered inside
evidence: Possibly building "D2" of the 1885 bird's-eye view, triangulated from three photos (SHSND 00042-00071, 00042-00195 and the c.1905 postcard 00259-00003; the three sight lines agree within 0.5 degrees). Triangulated from two or more solved photos; sight lines cross within about 1-3 m, so the position is good to roughly +/-10 m once picking error is allowed for. Why Roberts Hall: two full stories about 80 ft long as scaled from the photo (the footprint uses the Cow Boy's 24 x 75) with few upper windows (a hall, not hotel rooms), a raised front on its south end, long axis north-south; still standing about 1905 (Roberts Hall stood until 1923, while the hotel burned in 1897); next to today's Old Town Hall Theater (Roberts Hall may be the "town hall" of a 1903 stereo, still to be checked); near the hotel and in view of the railroad (HMdb).
sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-05-01, 1884-06-26; HMdb 88016; HAG (Medora chapter); Dickinson Press 1885-01-17
photos: houghton:3013539 ("Bill Williams' saloon," 1919) ; shsnd:00042-00071 (1885 bird's-eye, camera solved); shsnd:00042-00195 (1885-86 overview, camera solved); shsnd:00259-00003 (c.1905 postcard, camera solved)
notes: HAG's "Bill Williams" is a pseudonym. Roberts & Co.'s saloon at Medora burned Jan 1885 (Dickinson Press) - HAG says the first saloon "near Joe's store" burned before the move into the two-story building. Treat the identification as a strong inference to verify. Location graded C because the identification is inferred and conflicts with the Cow Boy's "lot 7, block 17" (today's Block 17 is about 300 m southeast). The earlier placement on Block 17 is replaced; check the plat's block numbering on the high-resolution scan, and the 1919 Hagedorn photos (Houghton 3013539, 3013472-75), which should still show it.

name: Metropolitan Hotel (Rough Riders Hotel from 1901-03)
built_text: lumber arrived Dec 11, 1884; "ready for occupancy" Feb 12, 1885 (Cow Boy)
removed_text: closed 1886, reopened 1901; disassembled and replaced by a replica in 1963 (HMdb 87499)
use: hotel: bar room, office, dining room, wash and baggage rooms below; 16 sleeping rooms and parlor above
material: frame, drop siding (brick veneer planned, never added)
evidence: Same site as today's Rough Riders Hotel (HMdb 87499). Triangulated from three photos: the dark, flat-roofed two-story building with rows of windows in SHSND 00042-00071 ("J") and 00042-00195, and the same building, white-painted, in the c.1905 postcard (00259-00003), where it is the Rough Riders Hotel. The three sight lines agree within 0.06 degrees (in the 00042-00071 photo the reprojected base sits about 40 px below the picked base, a known depth bias of that camera at the north end of town). Triangulated from two or more solved photos; sight lines cross within about 1-3 m, so the position is good to roughly +/-10 m once picking error is allowed for. It stands about 30 m south of the centre of today's (much larger) Rough Riders complex, i.e. at its south end.
sources: HMdb 87499; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-02-12, 1885-07-02; SAH ND-01-BI1; HAG plate caption; BROOKS57 ; SHSND 00042-00071, 00042-00195, 00259-00003 (camera solutions, docs/photo-matching.md)
photos: houghton:3013530; houghton:3013598 (1919); trc:o277182; trc:o277198; trc:o277180 (1963 before/during demolition) ; shsnd:00042-00071 (1885 bird's-eye, camera solved); shsnd:00042-00195 (1885-86 overview, camera solved); shsnd:00259-00003 (c.1905 postcard, camera solved)
notes: Date conflict: 1884 (SAH) vs 1885 (NPS handbook); the Cow Boy shows it opened Feb 1885. Renaming: 1901 (HMdb) vs 1903 (SAH). Brick veneer and a long front porch were planned. Landlord J. B. Walker from Oct 15, 1885. The 1957 photo (BROOKS57) shows about 10 by 4 window bays, consistent with 35x80. Leave the later 1-story end wing and asphalt siding out of an 1885 model.

name: Joe Ferris's store
aka: Ferris Inn / Joe Ferris General Store
built_text: cellar 25x60 and store 25x75 begun June 1885 on his Main Street lot; opened Aug 13, 1885 with the second story unfinished (Cow Boy); medora.com gives Aug 4
use: general store; family quarters upstairs; T.R. kept a room (SE corner upstairs)
evidence: Standing (rebuilt to the original plan in the 1960s per KFYR 2025). A feed stable stood behind it (HMdb 88062).
photos: houghton:3013537; houghton:3013655 (c.1919-20); trc:o292512 (1890s, marked X); trc:o277205 (1964) ; shsnd:00042-00071 (1885 bird's-eye, camera solved)
notes: Nearly burned in the fire of early 1887 (Eaton to Sewall, Feb 26, 1887). "Best store building in Medora" (Cow Boy). BROOKS57: exterior stair on the side wall to a second-floor door; T.R. stayed in the southeast corner room upstairs. Feed stable with Fisher behind the grocery (Nov 1885). 1885 photo: a two-story gabled building ("H") back-projects within about 25 m of this placement; its match in the other photos is not certain, so it is not triangulated.

name: St. Mary's Catholic Church
built_text: contract July 1884 (Peter Book); cornerstone Sept 20, 1884 (stone dated Sept 15); blessed Nov 2, 1884
material: yellow brick, common bond; wood-shingled gable roof; open wooden belfry with pyramidal roof
evidence: Standing on its original site at Fourth Street and Third Avenue; facade faces west (NRHP photos).
sources: NRHP 77001017; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-09-25; HMdb 88001
notes: Rear chimney (1941), bell (1946) and interior changes are later.

name: Von Hoffman House
built_text: commissioned Aug 1884; Peter Book
material: common-bond brick; hip-gabled wood-shingle roof; front porch
evidence: Lots 7-10, Block 15, Original Plat, at Broadway and Fifth Street (NRHP) - matches today's Block 15 parcels exactly. This is the link that ties the plat to today's grid.

name: Brick cottages (core of the old Billings County courthouse)
built_text: two brick cottages for the company, finished and accepted Nov 6, 1884 (Cow Boy)
use: de Mores rental houses; later courthouse and jail
evidence: Lots 13-18, Block 18 (NRHP 77001016). BROOKS57 argues the brick wings are 1884 Medora-brick cottages; NRHP says the wings were added later. Conflict open.
sources: NRHP 77001016; BROOKS57; HMdb 88030; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-09-25 ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-11-06; BROOKS57 pp. 29-32
notes: Lived in by the Hannigans and the Fortiers. Hipped roofs like the Von Hoffman House (BROOKS57). A central frame addition in the early 1900s made them the courthouse wings. SHSND 00042-00176 (1883-86) shows the Von Hoffman House with a one-story, low-roofed house with a front porch to its right against the east bluff - probably one of the brick cottages. BROOKS57 Fig. 13 ("Medora 1886") shows the two cottages; Fig. 8 (about 1900) labels the court house.

name: Dr. H. M. Jorgens's drug store
built_text: store on the corner by Oct 1884; new 21x32 building with full glass front April 1885
evidence: Opened "on the corner of Third avenue and Third street" in Nov 1884 (Cow Boy); HMdb 88066 puts a drug store on the NW corner of 3rd Street. Placed on the NW corner of today's 3rd Ave and 3rd St. The new 21x32 building of April 1885 has no stated location.
sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-10-16, 1885-04-16; HMdb 88066
notes: Earlier (Sept 1884) a temporary building moved "next to the company's store." The old "historical shack" was later rented to a clothing store (Cow Boy).

name: J. C. Fisher's two stores
built_text: being built Nov 1884
evidence: "two stores on Third Ave near Main St" (Cow Boy 1884-11-06).
notes: First planned May 1884 with Van Driesche as a three-store-room building. Tenants: Charles Cook, confectioner, and J. D. Garver, tinsmith (Nov 1884); later the Willard & Keeler meat market and Wells Fargo office (Dec 1885).

name: Fisher's roller rink and shooting gallery
built_text: planned Feb 1885; opened with a ball March 11, 1885
use: roller rink; church services held there 1885
evidence: "next to Joe's store, opposite the office of the Bad Lands Cowboy" (HAG). The Cow Boy's 1886 fire warning runs along Main Street from Mrs. Malloy's hotel to Bob Roberts's saloon (which moved into "the old skating rink" in Aug 1885), so both were on the Ferris block. Placed north of the store on Main Street.
sources: HAG (Medora chapter); Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-02-12, 1885-04-16; Dickinson Press 1885-03-14 ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-08, 1886-03-25
notes: Built by Jim Butler; opened about March 11, 1885; post office briefly inside; church services held there. From Aug 1885 it was Bob Roberts's saloon - ceiled, papered, painted, glass front (Cow Boy).

name: Bad Lands Cow Boy office
built_text: paper began Feb 1884 (masthead "Little Missouri, Medora P.O."); "Published in Medora" from Nov 1885
evidence: Opposite Fisher's rink and Joe Ferris's store (HAG) - placed across Main Street. A saloon stood "next door to the Cow Boy office" and a frame building to rent south of it (Cow Boy 1884-04-24).
sources: HAG; LOC sn84024777; HMdb 88045; Eaton to Sewall 1887-02-26 (TRC o292533)
notes: Painted April 1884 (Cow Boy).

name: Paddock's livery stable (Medora)
built_text: described Feb 1885
removed_text: Paddock's buildings shipped to Dickinson by flat car, June 1887
material: frame; drop siding; battlement front; 2-in floor
evidence: "on Third St between Third Ave and Broadway" (Cow Boy 1885-02-26). Side of the street not stated; placed west side.
sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-02-26; Dickinson Press 1887-06-04; HAG ; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-04-16, 1885-04-30, 1885-05-14
notes: Built by Jim Butler, finished April 16, 1885; size to be doubled (April 30). Livery office was the 1886 polling place. Paddock also moved Fitzgerald's old west-side dwelling next to his barn as Fred Banan's barber shop (May 1885).

name: Black Hills freight house (Medora & Black Hills Forwarding Co.)
built_text: sills laid July 1884; nearly finished Aug 1884
use: freight warehouse for the Deadwood stage and freight line
evidence: "on the south side of the track near the bluff... as near as possible to the butte," built "across Quick creek" (Cow Boy 1884-05-01, 05-08, 1886-05-13). Quick creek not yet identified; placed south of the track east of the depot.
sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-05-01, 1884-07-17; Dickinson Press 1884-07-12; Bismarck Weekly Tribune 1884-08-08; HAG ("well-built, substantial")
notes: Held 225 carloads; west end split into three rooms with a platform and derrick (Aug 1884); J. C. Fisher's office partitioned off inside (Sept 1884); underpinned May 1886.

name: Peter Book's brickyard
built_text: opened spring 1884; first kiln fired May 21, 1884
use: brickworks (10,000+ bricks a day; dark red brick)
evidence: "south of town where the Deadwood trail separates from the river" (Cow Boy 1884-04-24); ".9 of a mile south by river road from U.S. Highway 10 at Medora on the east bank... Section 34" (BROOKS57 p. 33). Placed in Sec. 34 about 0.9 mi south.
notes: Book patented a "lignite kiln" (1885). Book's house near the kiln, to be brick-veneered (1885); lime burned just west of the kiln (1885); a side-track along the bluff to the yard was planned (1885). New stockyards were built at "the brick-kiln butte" in Oct 1885 (Cow Boy).

name: Packing plant: main packing-house foundation
built_text: new plant, spring 1885
material: heavy timber frame on sandstone and brick foundations
footprint_ft: ~110-130 x 14-24 as drawn in 1956-57 (foundation remnant); NRHP gives the abattoir as 105 x 180
evidence: Long east-west foundation drawn about 100-125 ft south-southeast of the chimney on both 1950s NPS plans; scaled from the 1957 Tour map.
sources: NPS "Tour of Medora" map, Aug 1957 (NMP-TR-7008, in NPSHB 1962 p. 54, 0-600 ft scale); 1956 site plan NMP-TR 3002-A (BROOKS57 Fig. 6); NRHP 75001300; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12-04

name: Packing plant: ice house
built_text: company ice houses held 4,000 tons by Dec 1884, about 10,000 tons by Jan 1886 (Cow Boy)
footprint_ft: ~107 x 43 as drawn in 1957; NRHP: three ice houses 40 x 100
evidence: Dashed "ICE HOUSE" outline about 210 ft west-southwest of the chimney on the 1957 Tour map. NRHP says three ice houses adjoined the plant; only one is drawn.
sources: NPS "Tour of Medora" map, Aug 1957 (NMP-TR-7008, in NPSHB 1962 p. 54, 0-600 ft scale); 1956 site plan NMP-TR 3002-A (BROOKS57 Fig. 6); NRHP 75001300; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12-04; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12, 1886-01
notes: 1885 photo: the plant's large building back-projects within about 15 m of this placement (docs/photo-matching.md).

name: Packing plant: building east of the chimney (unidentified)
built_text: part of the 1885 plant (inferred)
use: unknown - perhaps refrigerator or cooling building
evidence: Unlabelled dashed rectangle about 195 ft east of the chimney on the 1957 Tour map. Cow Boy (Dec 1884): main refrigerator building 40x130, corridor about 36x180, passage 18x80.
sources: NPS "Tour of Medora" map, Aug 1957 (NMP-TR-7008, in NPSHB 1962 p. 54, 0-600 ft scale); 1956 site plan NMP-TR 3002-A (BROOKS57 Fig. 6); NRHP 75001300; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12-04

name: Packing plant: holding pens
evidence: Dash-dot enclosure divided into 4-5 pens about 840 ft northeast of the chimney on the 1957 Tour map and 1956 site plan.
sources: NPS "Tour of Medora" map, Aug 1957 (NMP-TR-7008, in NPSHB 1962 p. 54, 0-600 ft scale); 1956 site plan NMP-TR 3002-A (BROOKS57 Fig. 6); NRHP 75001300; Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-12-04

name: The Marquis's dam (ice pond)
built_text: built May 1884 just below the railroad bridge; rebuilt with flood-gates Oct 1885
use: ice harvesting; protected the slaughter house
evidence: "below the railroad bridge" (Cow Boy 1884-05-08); the river flows north, so below = just north of the bridge. Huffman's 1886 "Packing House" shows a pond in front of the plant.
sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884-05-08, 1885-10-22; HAG

name: Mrs. Malloy's hotel (Medora)
built_text: built on one of Joe Ferris's lots on Main Street; Mrs. Malloy moved in July 15, 1885
removed_text: "the Malloy building at Medora" torn down and moved to Dickinson, June 1887
evidence: On Main Street on a Ferris lot (Cow Boy 1885-07-16). The 1886 fire warning ran "between Mrs. Malloy's hotel and Bob Roberts' saloon," so it is placed at the other end of the Ferris block.
sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-07-16, 1886-03-25, 1886-10; Dickinson Press 1887-06-18
notes: Taken over by Arch Boyd Oct 1886.

name: John Kiefer's house
built_text: built about June 1885 on Third Avenue
evidence: Lots 13-14, Block 9, foreclosed 1886 (Cow Boy); house on Third Avenue (Cow Boy 1885-06). Placed on today's Block 9 lots 13-18 parcel.
sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1885-06, 1886

name: Pioneer Hotel, Little Missouri
built_text: advertised 1884
evidence: "close to the depot" (Cow Boy ad, 1884). Placeholder near the depot.
sources: Bad Lands Cow Boy 1884

name: Tiser House ("only original building of the town of Little Missouri")
built_text: dated by old-timers to 1881-86 (BROOKS57)
evidence: "about .1 of a mile west of the Medora bridge" in 1957 (BROOKS57 p. 32). Placed roughly 0.1 mi west of the river on the north side; the 1957 bridge position needs fixing from the 1957-62 aerials.
sources: BROOKS57 p. 32
notes: Standing in 1957, occupied by the Ira Tiser family.

name: Medora Stage & Forwarding Co. buildings (probable): three matching gabled buildings
built_text: stage line ran Oct 1884-May 1885 (HMdb 88033, 303699); buildings standing in the 1885 photos
use: office, warehouse and baggage room of the Medora-Deadwood stage line (NPSHB), if the identification holds
evidence: Building group "E" of the 1885 bird's-eye view, triangulated from SHSND 00042-00071 and 00042-00195. Triangulated from two or more solved photos; sight lines cross within about 1-3 m, so the position is good to roughly +/-10 m once picking error is allowed for. Three matching front-gabled buildings facing east, on the west side of Main Street.
sources: SHSND 00042-00071, 00042-00195; HMdb 88033, 303699; NPSHB p. 58 and the 1957 NPS "Tour of Medora" map (site 3); BROOKS57 pp. 19, 22 and Fig. 8
photos: shsnd:00042-00071 (1885 bird's-eye, camera solved); shsnd:00042-00195 (1885-86 overview, camera solved)
notes: Identification is inferred: the 1957 Tour map puts the Medora Stage & Forwarding Co. (described as three buildings - office, warehouse and baggage room) on the small triangular block west of De Mores Memorial Park, which is where this group stands. In 1957 one stood on its original site and two had been moved a few feet (BROOKS57 pp. 19, 22). Location graded C because it rests on this identification.

name: De Mores company office and store (NPRC store, post office, meat market, offices)
evidence: Photographed winter 1883-84 (houghton:3013533); labelled "company store" in the 1919 panorama. Former carriage-house store room (Cow Boy 1884-05-15); plank sidewalk in front of "the Co's stores" (1885-02-05); Howe scales in front of the offices (1885-06-25); NPRC general offices moved here from St. Paul, Oct 1885.

name: Medora Hotel (Coleman & Brown boarding house and restaurant)
evidence: Lot bought June 19, 1884; nearly done July 3; ad Nov 20, 1884 (Cow Boy).

name: Company barn, stable and corral (Deffebach livery)
evidence: Rented to Bassie Deffebach as a livery (May 1884); additional barn south of the old one (March 1885) (Cow Boy).

name: Gill Kennedy's oyster restaurant
evidence: Building moved from the west side to John Warn's old lot, Sept 1885; ice-house south of it (Cow Boy).

name: John O'Sullivan's barber shop and house
evidence: Lot 11, Block 19 (Cow Boy 1885-09), "next to John Warn's" restaurant. Block 19 is not in today's parcel layer.

name: McKenzie & O'Brien blacksmith shop
evidence: Moved to the north side of the track, May 1885; sold to Alex Morton 1886 (Cow Boy).

name: W. B. Pryor's shoe shop
evidence: On a lot "near the church," March-April 1885 (Cow Boy).

name: C. F. Ellison's house by the Catholic church
evidence: Cow Boy, Nov-Dec 1885.

name: NP coal mine and powder house
evidence: Coal mine roof caving in (Cow Boy 1884-06-12); old powder-house north of the track.

name: Merchants National Bank (planned)
evidence: Four lots at the corner of Third Street and Broadway bought April 1884; again planned "on the vacant hotel square" in 1885; never reported built (Cow Boy).

name: Medora school
evidence: "A new school building has been erected" (Bismarck Weekly Tribune 1885-11-20); photo shsnd:00042-00037 "new schoolhouse".

name: Stockyards
evidence: Old NP yards "across the river" were too small; a small yard 50x50, then 100x100 (Cow Boy 1885-04-16); new yards at "the brick-kiln butte" with the river, butte and railroad as pen walls (Oct 1885).

name: Paddock's building for the Boston clothing house
evidence: Nearly finished June 1885 (Cow Boy 1885-06-25); Paddock's residence moved to Dickinson in sections June 1887.

name: Sylvane Ferris's house
evidence: Two-story section with bay window and porch wing (shsnd:00129-00012).

name: De Mores rental houses ("Houses to be let")
evidence: shsnd:00042-00030 etc.; St. Paul Daily Globe 1884-02-13 mentions "numerous small residence houses."

name: De Mores brick business block (planned)
evidence: Two store rooms below, offices above (St. Paul Daily Globe 1884-02-13). Was it built?

name: Railroad shipping corrals
evidence: "the shipping corrals near the Cantonment" (HAG).

name: Gifford Bros. & Co. general store, Little Missouri
evidence: To open June 1883 (Dickinson Press 1883-06-16).

name: Other 1883 Little Missouri saloons (Smith & Stevens; Edgar & Saebastian; J. J. Smith)
evidence: Dickinson Press ads, July 1883.

name: Paddock's cabin and livery, Little Missouri
evidence: "'Little Misery.' Paddock's cabin in foreground, 1880" (Haynes, in NPSHB).
